1.why: All seven screens show only static content (headings, fields, buttons, and an inline Logs panel) with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups observed.

2.why: The active stepper pill, solid teal primary buttons, bold headings, and tinted status banners make the important elements visually dominant on every screen.

3.why: Fields, buttons, and the 'Need help?' link sit in one simple column, but the recovery and MFA codes the user needs are buried in a dense Logs block next to a very long token URL.

4.why: The always-visible five-step stepper, the persistent 'You can pause at any time. There is no session countdown' note, and codes that remain on screen mean the user never has to hold steps or rules in memory.

5.why: No screen offers a password-manager hint, autofill support, or a 'remember me' checkbox; the sign-in page shows only a bare password field and a Sign in button.

6.why: The identical header, stepper, banner style, and Logs panel on every step make familiar elements easy to recognize and messages like 'Password saved' confirm stored state, though the user's own email is never shown back.

7.why: Instructional prose is short and plain (e.g., 'Start when you are ready'), but the user must also read very long hexadecimal codes and URLs inside the Logs panel.

8.why: No error state ever appears in the screenshots, only success banners, so there is no observable evidence of how an error would describe the problem and its fix.

9.why: Nowhere is a sample input or worked example shown; the password step states rules ('Use 12 or more characters...') but never shows an example of what to type.

10.why: The flow is a single fixed path (email, code, password, sign-in, MFA) and never presents alternative authentication choices such as face login, so no such choices exist to be clear.

11.why: Each screen presents at most one primary action plus a single secondary option (e.g., 'Verify code' and 'Send a new recovery code'), never too many choices at once.

12.why: Every action is followed by an explicit tinted banner stating the outcome: 'Code verified', 'Password saved', 'Identity confirmed', and 'Privacy statement accepted'.

13.why: Each new step opens with a one-line guiding tip (e.g., 'Enter the verification code shown in the Logs panel') and a persistent, visible 'Need help?' link.

14.why: The 'Send a new recovery code' button, the reassurance that 'this step will stay here until you are ready', and the gentle rate-limit note support trying again, though a failed-entry retry screen is not shown.

15.why: Every step reuses the same layout, colors, stepper, banner style, and button design, so the interface is highly consistent and learnable over time.
